F01.P1.note: const n: i32 = 7; return n; — immutable binding, no annotation needed beyond literal typing.

F01.P2.note: var counter: i64 = 0; const LIMIT: i64 = 100; at file scope — mutable var vs immutable const clearly distinguished.

F02.P1.note: var v: i32 = undefined; then definite assignment on both branches of an if; Zig's `undefined` is the documented explicit uninitialized-storage marker satisfying R9's non-placeholder requirement (uninitialized is a first-class concept, not a hidden zero-fill).

F02.P2.note: var buf: [16]u8 = undefined; — genuinely uninitialized buffer, documented Zig mechanism distinct from zero-init.

F03.P1.note: x += 1; — compound assignment, checked-overflow in ReleaseSafe (ub/trap semantics documented).

F03.P2.note: xs.items[1] = 42; on std.ArrayList(i32) mutates backing slice in place.

F04.P1.note: const port = &slot; port.* = 9; — explicit pointer alias with write-through, dereference required by syntax.

F04.P2.note: const window = xs.items[0..]; — non-copying slice view over existing storage; slices are documented as non-owning views.

F04.P3.note: Pointer/reference equality via `==` on pointers to a heap-allocated struct — distinguishes identity from value equality; routing through a one-element array-list and reading back preserves the pointer for the identity test.

F05.P1.note: f(x) bare call — Zig has no implicit reference passing for aggregate value types at an ordinary call site; ArrayList passed by value is a struct copy of the descriptor, elements are heap-shared depending on type, expressible and buildable.

F05.P2.note: fn put(cell: *i32) void { cell.* = 12; } — explicit pointer parameter required by the language for caller-writable scalar access.

F05.P3.note: Zig has no lexical closures: a nested function cannot capture a variable (`k`) from its enclosing function scope; only top-level/comptime-parameterized functions exist, and capturing state requires passing it explicitly as an argument/struct field, which the canonical_task's numbered sub-requirement (2) explicitly forbids (capture, not parameter passing). No documented mechanism satisfies sub-requirement (1); citation: Zig language reference, functions section — no closures/anonymous capturing functions are supported.

F06.P1.note: fn mid(xs: []const i32) i32 { return xs[1]; } — returns a value (i32), independent of the slice, buildable.

F06.P2.note: Zig supports returning an anonymous struct/tuple-like aggregate: fn divmod2(a,b: i32) struct{q:i32,r:i32} — destructure at call site.

F07.P1.note: const r = a * b + c; ordinary precedence, checked-overflow semantics under ReleaseSafe.

F07.P2.note: Zig requires explicit @divTrunc/@mod builtins for integer division/remainder (no bare `/` on ints without exactness guarantee) and @as(f64,...) conversions for float division — all explicit, buildable.

F08.P1.note: @addWithOverflow(m, 1) returns a struct with overflow flag (rung akin to (i), substituting 0 on overflow) — behavior fully determinable from the construct; ReleaseSafe plain `+` traps deterministically as a fallback rung (iv).

F08.P2.note: P-a: no standard checked-division-returning-optional exists in Zig's std library; only an explicit local `if (b == 0)` guard (rung ii) is available, substituting a weaker mechanism than a first-class optional-returning divide.

F09.P1.note: std.mem.eql(u8, s1, s2) — documented contents comparison, unambiguously not identity comparison.

F09.P2.note: std.sort.sort/std.mem.sort with an explicit descending comparator function value sorts the slice in place (documented in-place mutation, no allocation).

F10.P1.note: std.math.cast(i32, big) returns ?i32 (rung i, checked conversion yielding optional) — explicit, documented.

F10.P2.note: Zig requires explicit @as(f64, i) / @floatFromInt(i) conversion before adding to a float; no implicit int-to-float promotion exists.

F11.P1.note: xs[i] traps deterministically on out-of-range index under the frozen ReleaseSafe recipe (documented bounds-check behavior); std.mem provides no separate checked-optional indexed read as a competing form.

F11.P2.note: xs[1..4] slice syntax shares storage with the original array/slice (documented non-copying view).

F12.P1.note: var o: ?i32 = null; const n = o orelse 0; — optional type in the type signature and standard coalescing operator `orelse`.

F12.P2.note: P-a: Zig's std library has no Optional.map/andThen chaining combinator; the canonical_task's non-if requirement can only be met by writing the explicit `if (o) |v| ... else null` unwrap form, the named R9 substitution.

F13.P1.note: std.fmt.parseInt returns an error union (![]u8->!i32); `try` propagates the failure to the caller, and the function's own return type (!i32) documents fallibility.

F13.P2.note: std.fmt.parseInt(...) catch 0; — standard local error-handling operator with an explicit fallback value.

F14.P1.note: union(enum) { Circle: f64, Rect: struct{w:f64,h:f64} } is a closed, exhaustive tagged union; the compiler forbids adding a case elsewhere.

F14.P2.note: switch (s) on the tagged union with no else arm is compiler-checked for exhaustiveness (compile error on missing case).

F14.P3.note: P-a: Zig's tagged unions are closed by design and cannot be extended from a separate unit; the only standard substitute for open extension is a hand-written vtable pattern (a struct of function pointers implemented per-type), which is a weaker, manually maintained mechanism rather than a first-class extensible dispatch construct.

F15.P1.note: fn head(comptime T: type, xs: []const T) T { return xs[0]; } — declaration-level parametric type T with a statically recoverable T->T result relationship, reused at i32 and []const u8.

F15.P2.note: P-a/P-c: Zig has no declaration-site trait/interface constraint syntax; a generic function's requirements are enforced only structurally at instantiation via comptime duck-typing, so misuse is diagnosed at the call/instantiation site, not at the generic's own declaration as the canonical_task requires.

F15.P3.note: P-a: Zig has no interface/abstract-type runtime dispatch mechanism; heterogeneous runtime dispatch over two concrete types behind one declared element type must be hand-built with an explicit vtable struct (function pointers + opaque/erased pointer), a substituted weaker mechanism rather than a first-class abstract element type.

F16.P1.note: std.ArrayList(i32) literal-style init plus a for-loop summing elements (no single-call fold/sum combinator in std, so the explicit iteration form is the R10-selected minimal form).

F16.P2.note: std.StringHashMap(i32) with an iterator for entries, and .get("b") orelse 0 for the missing-key fallback lookup.

F17.P1.note: defer file.close(); immediately after a successful open guarantees release on every exit path including the failure path of the subsequent read, per Zig's documented defer semantics (always runs at scope exit, LIFO).

F17.P2.note: P-a: Zig has no automatic end-of-lifetime hook (no destructors/drop); a user type's cleanup (incrementing `released`) must be invoked explicitly via `defer h.deinit();` at the call site rather than triggered automatically by the language at scope exit, the named R9-style substitution for a deterministic destructor.

F18.P1.note: const std = @import("std"); std.debug.print("x\n", .{}); — import introduces `std` into scope, output statement is standard.

F18.P2.note: `pub fn pub_add` vs a non-`pub` `fn secret` in a `util.zig` module/file; `secret` is compiler-enforced unreachable outside the file; external call via `util.pub_add(2,3)` after `@import("util.zig")`, using the frozen multi-unit recipe.

F19.P1.note: std.Thread.spawn for two threads computing 20 and 22, .join() on both, summing results — Zig's current (post-async-removal) standard concurrency facility is OS threads via std.Thread, which is a standard, toolchain-shipped mechanism.

F19.P2.note: std.Thread.Mutex guarding the shared i64 counter across two threads each incrementing 1000 times, joined before reading the final value — documented race-free discipline via an explicit lock, verifiable in principle by repeated runs.

F20.P1.note: extern fn abs(x: c_int) c_int; declared and linked against libc per the frozen recipe (Zig's built-in C FFI, no third-party binding generator).

F20.P2.note: export fn add2(a: c_int, b: c_int) c_int { return a + b; } — Zig's `export` keyword produces a C-ABI, unmangled external symbol directly, per language documentation.
